activity_context.topic_title: The Average Value of a Function

examples.knowledge_point: Finding an Interval Given the Average Value of a Function
examples.problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $g(x) = 3 x$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $3.$
examples.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}3x\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}){|}_{0}^{c} \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{c}^{2}}{2}-0) \\ 3 & =\frac{3c}{2} \\ c & =2\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Within the interval $[-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}],$ determine the average value of $g(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡3x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\frac{\pi }{2}-(-\frac{\pi }{2})}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }[(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}))-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2}))+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2})))] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }[(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{3\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{3\pi }{2}))] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }[(0+(-1))-(0+1)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }(-2) \\  & =\frac{2}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
